implementation_notes: Scala's standard library has mutable.Queue, a FIFO collection over ArrayDeque whose enqueue/dequeue pair is the single-threaded event queue; on the JVM it inherits java.util.concurrent.BlockingQueue for the concurrent case, and actor or stream libraries (Akka, Pekko, fs2) build mailbox-style queues on top. What replaces the classic structure is the collection plus a drain point - dequeue in a loop until empty, usually once per simulation tick - while the classic explicit queue is still justified when events must be coalesced or stored in a fixed ring.
pitfalls: mutable.Queue is not thread-safe and exposes the mutable ArrayDeque underneath - sharing one across threads needs explicit synchronization or a JVM BlockingQueue.
dequeue on an empty queue throws NoSuchElementException; drain with nonEmpty/dequeueFirst or headOption rather than assuming an item is there.
Enqueuing from a handler while draining extends the same loop and can starve the tick - cap the drain or route re-posts to the next cycle.
